gen-gf-gabarito-gf-alyamama: Gabarito draws every stroke with one nib, its open terminals letting the counters flow outward without a hairline in sight. And Alyamama, a classic serif, brings a soft thick-thin shift with well-spaced curve endings, so a long page keeps moving gently.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-ancizar-serif: Ancizar Serif reads bookish and editorial, its modest contrast recalling lightly engraved brass, with a c that gapes wide at any size. Gabarito sits beside it like a ruler-drawn line, constant in width and noticeably more expressive.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-andada-pro: Neon-tube consistency runs through every stroke of Gabarito, with terminals cut open so its counters flow outward. But Andada Pro, a text serif, sits in the middle ground with moderate modulation, and the two make a lively, bookish mix.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-aref-ruqaa: Loose, friendly and a little theatrical, Gabarito draws its letters with no thick-thin pulse at all, while Aref Ruqaa, a classic serif, keeps hairlines neither wispy nor heavy. Dignity meets personality.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-aref-ruqaa-ink: Aref Ruqaa Ink is a text serif with literary poise. Gabarito, drawn with one nib and none of a brush stroke's pressure swelling, makes a heading that turns bold but weak if shrunk down small, whereas the body keeps its open apertures.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-average: Marker-like and full of character, Gabarito keeps a constant-width line with open terminals. Average, a classic serif, adds the faint reed-pen thickening of its curves and gaping e, so a long passage feels literary and authoritative.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-besley: Besley reads dignified and editorial, its c curve staying far from closing. Gabarito does its best work as a bold, flowing display voice with no brush swelling, while Besley handles the comfortable contrast of steady text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-biz-udpmincho: Bent neon tubing, more or less, in Gabarito's constant-thickness letters and open terminals. And BIZ UDPMincho, a serif, tapers gently from stem to joint, with gaps that stop letters from crowding, so the two sit together with ease.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-bona-nova-sc: Bona Nova SC is refined and classic, its small counters unclogged and its thin strokes just lighter than thick. Yet Gabarito is the one to catch the eye, its flat, unswelling line running along every open-terminal curve.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-brawler: Gabarito draws a ruler-straight, constant-width line with open terminals. Brawler, a serif, answers in a literary way, with clear openings in its rounded letters and a measured thick-thin ratio, so Gabarito earns its keep big and short.
